notes: Verdict: 9,155 does not appear in the Franklin et al. 2020 main text, which prints no figure for Europe or any European region; supplementary table S1, where the regional values live, could not be opened by automated fetch (PMC, BMJ and Europe PMC all refuse), so whether 9,155 matches any S1 row remains unresolved. No S1 value or caption is reported here because none was seen. What was established from opened sources: (1) The ledger's global figure is exactly as printed in the full text: 295 210 (284 493 to 306 187) deaths in 2017, age-standardised 4.0 (3.8 to 4.1) per 100,000, 44.5% fewer deaths than 1990 (Brunel repository copy of the full text; IHME library page). (2) The main text says S1 provides all-age drowning-specific deaths and age-standardised cause-specific mortality rates for 1990 and 2017 with percentage change for every country, region and super-region in the GBD 2017 location hierarchy, and S2 the same for YLLs. WHO regions are not part of that hierarchy as the paper describes it, so a WHO European Region row is not expected in S1 (judgment, grade D); a GBD 2017 value for the WHO region, if wanted, would have to come from the GBD results tool rather than S1. (3) The esanum article's regional figures carry WHO-region labels (Western Pacific about 83,000; South-East Asia about 83,000; Africa 77,000 at 5.7; Eastern Mediterranean 36,000; Americas 16,500; Europe 9,155 at 1.0, 3% of global) and are attributed to the WHO Global status report on drowning prevention 2024; only the global 295,210 is GBD-shaped. The 9,155 pair is therefore WHO-region-shaped and is unlikely to be a GBD 2017 regional estimate (judgment, grade D), consistent with the ledger's existing finding that the WHO report prints 15,000 and 1.7. (4) A published correction (injuryprev-2019-043484corr1, BMJ URL path dated 2020/09/28) changes authorship and affiliations only. (5) Citation confirmed from the journal's article-info page: Injury Prevention 2020;26:i83-i95, received 19 Sep 2019, accepted 6 Dec 2019, first published 20 Feb 2020. Caveats: full-text verification used the Brunel repository PDF (labelled FullText.pdf) because the BMJ article page and PDF would not open; the BMJ .long and .info pages did load and match it. The fetch tool returns converted text, so BMJ's supplementary file link (file name not visible) could not be read off the page. The new row for the global rate is a by-product; the fetch of the full text reported two different intervals for it (3.8 to 4.1 in the abstract, 3.6 to 4.1 in the Discussion), flagged in its scope. The url correction for gbd-2017-franklin is optional. No figure in this bundle comes from memory.
